what_it_proves: for each address, the body compared (the project's own, or a GENERATED module file when --source is given) and the ORIGINAL's machine code at that VA agree on the registers, the named flags and the named memory, over the entry states driven
what_it_does_not_prove: anything about other entry states, other addresses, or the game as a whole; there is no aggregate verdict

addresses.compares: eax and the bytes of every absolute guest address the generated body names (a plain-C body models its return value and the memory it writes, not the guest's other registers)
addresses.does_not_compare: the arithmetic flags: a plain-C body does not model the guest's flag state, which the original leaves as its last arithmetic instruction set it. Only a lifted body publishes one (RECOMP_FLAGS_OUT) and only it can be flag-compared.
addresses.verdict_meaning: eax (for a generated module) and the named memory both match

frame.note: no frame size was requested: frame traffic was NOT compared

input_set.seeded: each named address holds (case+1) on both sides - small values so a table index stays inside the mapped window and the reference machine runs the function rather than faulting on its own data; registers are per-case constants; esp is a stack page whose top word is the return sentinel
input_set.not_covered: any entry state other than these, any address the body does not name, and any input the game would supply
